daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR is accelerating work on the asset forfeiture bill, with passage targeted by December 2026. The legislation aims to strengthen the state's ability to seize illegally obtained assets. Meanwhile, controversy has emerged over the tenure of the National Police Chief, with Kompolnas warning of potential political intervention behind proposals to extend or modify the term, though one lawmaker defended it as the president's prerogative.

  • President Prabowo is touring multiple provinces to inspect forest fire response, having arrived in Pekanbaru amid heavy smoke and reportedly planning to reward officials for effective fire management.
  • An alliance of student groups plans to demonstrate at the DPR on 27 August with ten demands, amid reports that transactions on donation accounts have been suspended and buses of protesters were attacked.
  • Kompolnas has warned police that account freezing could damage bank reputations amid the controversy over blocked accounts tied to upcoming demonstrations.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs has strengthened cross-ministerial collaboration for local government awards, with four new categories aligned with Asta Cita.
  • A Gerindra official in Banyumas was found to have acted as intermediary in a Rp 650 million corruption case involving Unsoed university.
  • Groups from Kebumen and Bangkalan travelling to Jakarta shared similar narratives of supporting the president while raising concerns about food assistance programmes.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Giuseppe Garibaldi, Indonesia's prospective first aircraft carrier, has begun sailing toward Indonesia and will participate in the sailing pass for TNI's 81st anniversary. The Italian carrier is escorted by an Italian frigate, with two Indonesian warships ready to greet it upon entering Indonesian waters, and TNI AL says it will be used for humanitarian assistance. Indonesia's first aircraft carrier will debut at the TNI anniversary, while the carrier base enters its finishing phase.

  • PLN has partnered with the Navy to train personnel in the Sangihe Islands.

Other

President Prabowo has set an ambitious target for Indonesia to stop importing oil and LPG within three years. In parallel, the government launched a massive solar power initiative, with Indonesia setting a three-year target for 100 GW solar capacity, a project attracting US$62 billion in investment. The 100 GWp solar plant programme is expected to save the state Rp 73.9 trillion per year through reduced solar fuel imports and generate 5.5 million jobs with Rp 1,140 trillion investment. The government is also working to power off-grid villages with 100 GWp solar plants.

  • The death toll from the NTT earthquake has risen to 103 with 1,666 injured, with 24,597 homes heavily damaged and 185,113 displaced, and the Ministry of Social Affairs reporting that survivors are experiencing fear and anxiety.
  • President Prabowo hopes forest fires can be extinguished within two weeks, as burned area in Jambi increases and smoke worsens, prompting deployment of 665 TNI troops via two Boeing 737 aircraft to Kalimantan.
  • PLN is developing 1,000 MWp solar plants with battery storage in Bali to replace imported fuel oil.
  • The DPR and East Kalimantan aim to maximize oil and gas potential in the Mahakam block.
  • An expert advised that transmigration areas could power Indonesia's new economic hubs, described as "the right programme at the right time".
